A configuration eval's report never reaches the evidence store, so no learned change can cite it. `scripts/config-eval.mjs` is the only caller of `runEval` and keeps its report as a file under `~/.deepbuild/evals/`, named by the digest of the two variants. The learned layer's check (`replayCheck` in `packages/record/src/learned.ts`) reads the replays a change cites by `ev:<sha256>` handle, from the evidence store, and refuses a widening that cites none it holds. Nothing puts a report there: no file under `packages/*/src` or `scripts` stores one.

So the design's local-first step, a change widening to its session's repo on a replay it cites, can only be refused today unless a person stores the report by hand.

From the Nov 13 package audit (`reports/package-story-gpu-2026-11-13.md`). Sites are as read at `c56fe5407`; confirm each before changing it.

**Epic:** #8 · **Design:** [The learned layer](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#the-learned-layer) · [How we know version 0 works](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#how-we-know-version-0-works)

### Scope
- A finished eval's report (its frozen plan and its runs) is kept in the evidence store by hash, through the hub, and the run prints its handle
- The file under `~/.deepbuild/evals/` stays, since the preflight's config eval lane reads it
- No new command and no new option

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After an eval run, the evidence store holds the report's bytes, and the handle the run prints resolves to them: a test fails on the merge base, where the store holds nothing
- [ ] A `learn.widened` change by the local-first rule that cites that handle passes `replayCheck` when the report adopts, and is refused naming the outcome when it doesn't
- [ ] #112's and #1108's suites pass unchanged

### Proof
The store's contents after a run on the merge base and on the change, and the two suites' runs.

### Depends on
- none

The supervisor records what a run's sandbox refused as `sandbox.denied`, once per operation and target, and #2399 brings the egress filter under that rule. Nothing bounds how many different targets one run may have recorded. A run can make the target differ every time: a write tried at a new path in a loop, or a request to its egress filter under a new `Host`. Each adds an event, and the set the supervisor keeps in memory to tell them apart grows with them for as long as the run lives. A target is also recorded at whatever length it arrives. Called on its own on `main`, the egress filter reported a `Host` of 8,013 characters whole. The event's schema takes at most 8,192, and the supervisor drops an append that fails: a sandboxed run on `main` that sent its filter one request under a `Host` of 9,013 characters was answered 403, and no event was recorded for it. This gives a run a ceiling, says what was left out, and bounds a target's length.

**Epic:** #4 · **Design:** [Threats, and what stops each one](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#threats-and-what-stops-each-one) · [The event catalogue](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#the-event-catalogue)

**Runs on:** Any machine: the supervisor with a record and #1106's sample stack, and requests sent to the run's filter port.

### Scope
- A run has at most 256 `sandbox.denied` events naming what it was refused (a starting value). Past that, a refusal for a new operation and target is counted and not recorded, and the set kept in memory for the run stops growing
- When such a run ends, one more `sandbox.denied` for it says how many were left out: its operation is `more` and its target is the count, so the record never reads as if the run was refused only what it lists. A run under the ceiling gets no such event
- A target longer than 512 bytes (a starting value) is recorded as its first 512 bytes, cut at a character boundary, followed by its full length in bytes, so one past the schema's limit is recorded and never dropped
- The three paths that record the kind share the ceiling and the cut: the macOS log reader, the Linux sandbox parent and the egress filter
- Not in this task: a ceiling across runs; a change to the event's schema; and `sandbox.refused`, which a session's own sandbox reports

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With #1106's sample stack up, 1,000 plain HTTP requests sent to the run's filter port, each under a different `Host`, are each answered 403. The record holds 256 `sandbox.denied` events for the run naming a target, and after the run ends one more whose operation is `more` and whose target reads `744`. With #2399 in and this change out, the record gains 1,000, and this test fails
- [ ] A second thousand, under other names, adds no event while the run lives, and the closing event reads `1744`. A planted supervisor that starts a new 256 once the first is full records 512 and fails, naming the count
- [ ] A request whose `Host` is 9,000 characters long is answered 403 and recorded with a target of its first 512 bytes followed by `9000`. On the merge base no event is recorded for it, and this test fails
- [ ] A run refused 3 different targets records 3 events and no closing one. A planted supervisor that always writes the closing event writes `more` with `0` and fails, naming the run
- [ ] Two runs side by side, each sent 300 requests under different names, each record 256 and a closing `44`. A planted supervisor that keeps one count for both records 256 in all and fails, naming the second run

### Proof
The record's `sandbox.denied` events for each case, on the branch and with only #2399 in; the long target as recorded; the two runs' counts; and each planted twin with its failure.

### Depends on
- #2399 A run's egress filter records a refusal once per operation and target, as the sandbox does: a request refused in a loop no longer adds an event each time

An extension's `tool.before` handler has 500 ms to reply (`EXTENSION_HOOK_MS` in `packages/hub/src/wire.ts`), and the host waits 250 ms more for the trip back (`HOOK_GRACE_MS` in `packages/extension-host/src/host.ts`). A handler that misses it is failed for that call and its reply dropped, which is right for one slow call. The host's own comment says the rest: "a handler that misses it stays loaded, and its late reply goes nowhere". It is asked again on the next tool call, and the one after. An extension whose handler hangs therefore adds at least its 500 ms deadline to every tool call it is asked about, for as long as it is installed, and the only trace is a line on the hub's standard error (`deep hub: tool.before handler failed`, in `packages/hub/src/core.ts`). Nothing counts the failures, nothing is on the record, and nothing reaches you. Extensions an agent builds from one sentence arrive in R2 (#359), and one of those is the likeliest to hang. Read from the code on `main` at 53c0e72a; not run.

**Epic:** #6 · **Design:** [Extension API (TypeScript, in-process)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#extension-api-typescript-in-process) · [Hook protocol (deep-hook and the hub)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#hook-protocol-deep-hook-and-the-hub) · [States people see](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#states-people-see)

**Runs on:** Any machine. The budget reads the reference Mac

### Scope
- A handler's failure, a missed deadline or a throw, is on the record with its extension, its hook kind and the call it failed, and no longer only in the hub's log
- Three failures in a row by one extension on one hook kind set that handler aside: the host stops asking it, and a hook it would have answered takes the policy a failure takes today, at once and with no wait (the three is drafted)
- A reply in time clears the count. A handler stays set aside until its extension is restarted, updated or turned on again by you, or the hub starts, and each of those gives it one fresh try
- What is set aside is said with kinds that exist: one doctor item naming the extension, the hook kind and the last failure, and one reading on each session whose calls it would have judged, as a late answer leaves one today
- A deny a handler gave in time still stands, and the core's floor holds with any handler set aside, as it does in safe mode
- How the failure and the set-aside are recorded is the implementer's, under the event catalogue's rules
- Not in this task: a handler that is slow and in time; an extension's other calls, which have their own deadlines; a check kind's run; and turning an extension off, which stays yours

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test extension whose `tool.before` handler never replies: its first three tool calls each wait the deadline and are recorded as failed, and the fourth and every later one are answered with no wait for it, within 20 ms of a host with no such extension (drafted). The record holds the three failures and the set-aside. On the merge base the tenth call waits as long as the first and the record holds nothing, and the test fails, naming the tenth call's wait
- [ ] Two failures, a reply in time, then two more failures set nothing aside. A planted host that counts failures and never clears them sets the handler aside at the fourth failure and fails, naming the call
- [ ] With a handler set aside, `deep doctor` shows one item naming the extension, the hook kind and the last failure, and each session it would have judged holds one reading that says so. Restarting the extension clears the item, and its next call is asked again
- [ ] A second extension's deny on the same call stands on every one of those calls. With the done gate's own handler set aside, a claim citing a run the session never made still goes back, as in safe mode
- [ ] Budgets, on the reference Mac in the local preflight, compared with the merge base: a `tool.before` whose handlers all reply in time gains under 0.1 ms (drafted)

### Proof
The hanging handler's ten calls with their waits on the merge base and on the change, the record's events, the doctor item and the sessions' readings, and the planted host shown failing.

The event catalogue says `sandbox.denied` is recorded "once per operation and target". Two of the three places that record it keep to that: the macOS log reader and the Linux sandbox parent each skip a refusal whose run, operation and target they have already seen (`watchDenials` and `readDenials` in `packages/supervisor/src/supervisor.ts`). The third doesn't. A run that holds a credential with hosts gets an egress filter (#1106), and the supervisor appends an event for every refusal the filter reports, with no such check (`launch`, in the callback it hands `openEgress`). The filter listens on a port of this machine, and refuses plain HTTP and any tunnel to a host no credential names. On `main`, a sandboxed run started by the supervisor that sent its own filter the same plain request 50 times left 50 `sandbox.denied` events with one operation and one target. Called on its own, the filter reported 200 more for 200 requests that differed only in their `Host`. So a run whose code tries a refused request again and again, as a test suite does when its network is closed, adds an event for each try for as long as it runs, and so does anything else on this machine that finds the port.

**Epic:** #4 · **Design:** [Threats, and what stops each one](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#threats-and-what-stops-each-one) · [The event catalogue](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#the-event-catalogue)

**Runs on:** Any machine: the supervisor with #1106's sample stack, and requests sent to the run's filter port.

### Scope
- The supervisor records a refusal from a run's egress filter only when that run has had none recorded for the same operation and target, in the set the other two paths already keep, which is cleared when the run ends
- The filter answers every refused request as it does now, with a 403 or a refused tunnel: only what is recorded changes
- A stand-in refused for where it was put (#1106) is recorded as before, once for each placement and host
- Not in this task: a ceiling on how many different targets one run may have recorded (#2420); and who may connect to the filter's port

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With #1106's sample stack up, 100 identical plain HTTP requests sent to the run's filter port are each answered 403 and leave exactly one `sandbox.denied` for the run, with the operation `egress-plain-http` and that target. On the merge base the record gains 100, and this test fails
- [ ] 100 tunnels asked for to one host no credential names leave one `sandbox.denied` with the operation `egress-host`, and a tunnel to a second such host adds one more. A planted supervisor that keeps one refusal per operation records none for the second host and fails, naming the host
- [ ] #1106's third criterion runs unchanged and passes, and each of its three attempts sent a second time leaves the count of events as it was. A planted supervisor that records no refusal from the filter fails #1106's criterion, naming the placement
- [ ] A refusal recorded for one run doesn't hide the same operation and target for a second run beside it, and the first refusal of a run started after another ended is recorded. A planted supervisor that keeps the set without the run records none for the second run and fails, naming the run

### Proof
The record's `sandbox.denied` events for each case on the branch and on the merge base, where the hundred requests add a hundred; #1106's criterion's run; and each planted twin with its failure.

The transcript archive copies a session's transcript again whenever it has grown, and every copy handles the whole file. `copy()` in `packages/archive/src/index.ts` reads the file into memory, hashes it, turns it into one string, scrubs that string, stores the scrubbed text as a new piece of evidence, reads that back and hashes it again. The hub runs a pass when it starts and every hour (`packages/hub/src/core.ts`), in its own process. That holds for the transcripts the perf lane measures, which are 1 MB and 5 MB (`archive-live`, `archive-month`, `archive-backlog`). It doesn't hold for a long session. A probe of `main` at 53c0e72a took one Claude Code transcript, 94% of it tool results with one line of 2 MB, through three passes at 80, 90 and 100 MB. They took 7.3 s, 5.8 s and 8.4 s, the process served no timer for up to 1.2 s at a stretch, its resident memory peaked at 869 MB, 1,610 MB and 2,416 MB from 36 MB idle, and the evidence store gained three whole copies. At 540 MB the pass ends with `the archive pass left 1 copy undone`, from `Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters`, and stores nothing. It does so again every hour, and the line the hub writes to its standard error names neither the session nor the cause. So the sessions with the most in them cost the most to keep, and past 512 MiB they are never archived: once the agent deletes the transcript, the session is gone. Sessions this size are reported in the field: one of 160 turns and 2,383 tool calls measured 322 MB after nine hours. The probe ran the archive in a process of its own, with its record and evidence store, not in a live hub, so what a held hook waits during a pass was not measured.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [First-party extensions that ship on by default](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#first-party-extensions-that-ship-on-by-default) · [Evidence](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#evidence) · [Numbers version 0 has to hold](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#numbers-version-0-has-to-hold)

**Runs on:** Any machine. The budgets read the reference Mac

### Scope
- A pass on a transcript that only grew reads, scrubs and stores what it gained since its last copy. The session's archived transcript is its parts in order, and `session:` handles resolve across the parts as they do through one copy today
- A part ends at a line's end. What follows the last complete line waits for the next pass, and a tail still unchanged at that pass is copied as it stands, so no line is scrubbed in two halves and none is left out
- A transcript whose earlier bytes changed is copied again from its start, in parts of a bounded size, as one seen for the first time is. No step holds a whole transcript in memory
- The copy is the same text: the parts joined equal the transcript scrubbed whole
- How a part is recorded, as a new version of `transcript.archived` or beside it, is the implementer's, under the event catalogue's rules. The copy of one session on demand takes the same path
- Not in this task: the forge's CI logs; the text index (#1515); how long earlier whole copies are kept; and finding one session's file without walking every transcript (#2316)

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A Claude Code transcript of 100 MB, 94% of it tool results with one line of 2 MB, already archived, gains 1 MB. The pass that follows adds under 2 MB to the evidence store, ends within 1 s, raises the process's resident memory by under 64 MB, and the process serves a 5 ms timer at least every 50 ms throughout (the three limits are drafted). On the merge base the same pass takes 5.8 s or more, serves no timer for up to 1.2 s, peaks above 800 MB and stores a whole copy. A planted archive that reads the file whole fails, naming the peak
- [ ] A transcript of 600 MB, never archived, is copied in one pass: its parts read back in order equal the file scrubbed a line at a time, and `session:<id>#m<n>` resolves for its last message. On the merge base the pass says it left 1 copy undone and stores nothing
- [ ] A key pasted into a line that is half written when a pass runs is in no part in any form: that pass copies up to the last complete line, the next copies the rest, and the rotate ask is raised once. A planted archive that cuts at the file's end stores the key's first half in one part and fails, naming the part
- [ ] A transcript whose first megabyte was rewritten after its last copy is copied again from its start, and the session's handles resolve through the new parts. A planted archive that appends the rewritten file's tail to the old parts fails, naming the first line that differs
- [ ] For every transcript in #20's suite and its perf tasks, the parts joined are byte-identical to the one copy the merge base stores of the finished file, and a second pass over an unchanged transcript reads none of it
- [ ] Budgets, on the reference Mac in the local preflight, compared with the merge base: a new perf task holds the first criterion's pass, and `archive-live`, `archive-month` and `archive-backlog` stay within their limits

### Proof
The probe's three passes and its 540 MB pass shown on the merge base first, then the same runs on the change: the time, the longest stretch with no timer served, the peak resident memory and the evidence bytes of each pass. Then the half-written key, the rewritten file, and the joined parts beside the merge base's copies.

The hub takes a request ID on every app or CLI write with an effect (#1577), but no client sends one yet. So a phone that loses a reply and sends the answer again still writes it twice, and an undo made from a stale view still lands. Each write that `deep`, the app and the phone make should carry its request ID and the view it was made from, and keep both across its own retries.

**Epic:** #1571 · **Follows:** #1577 · **Design:** [Socket roles and contract versions](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#socket-roles-and-contract-versions) ("Reads and writes a slow link can afford")

### Scope
- **The app** (`crates/deep-app/src/answer.rs`, `send`): a request ID is drawn once per answer, before signing, and goes inside the params the signature covers. The re-pair retry and every resend of that answer reuse it
- **The app's other writes:** an undo, an overrule, a staged undo, a saved offer and a note each take a request ID and send `view`, the `log_pos` of the read the choice was made from
- **The CLI:** `deep inbox answer`, `deep inbox undo`, `deep inbox save` (`packages/hub/src/inbox.ts`), `deep memory overrule` (`memory.ts`) and `deep undo staged:<id>` (`undo.ts`) send a request ID. A reply cut off by a dropped socket is sent again once with the same ID
- **The replica** (`crates/deep-replica/src/drive/hubcopy.rs`): the copy of the hub answers `request` and `view` as the hub does
- A client shows a refusal at `/params/view` as the new state, with the change it names

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The app's answer, sent again after a cut reply, gets the first result, and the record holds one `ask.answered`
- [ ] `deep inbox answer` with its reply cut, then retried, ends with one `ask.answered`, and the command exits 0
- [ ] The app's undo of a default from a view that another device's answer has since overtaken is refused, and the app shows that answer
- [ ] The same request ID is never sent with two different params

### Proof
Each case on this branch and on the merge base.

Two linear scans on hot or growing paths, found by reading `origin/main` at `145315636`:

1. **Full event-log decode in `@deepbuild/buying` (`packages/buying/src/index.ts`):** `Buyer.sync()` calls `this.o.record.read({ after: this.cursor, limit: PAGE })` with no `kinds` filter, JSON-decoding every event appended to the record since the last `buy()` only to keep `e.kind === 'card_rule.set'`. Every other ledger/table fold (`leases`, `budget`, `runner`, `supervisor`) uses `readSince(record, cursor, ['card_rule.set'], ...)` so SQLite filters by `(kind, log_pos)` index without decoding unrelated events and advances the cursor to the log head.
2. **Full transcript-tree walk on held pushes in `@deepbuild/archive` (`packages/archive/src/index.ts`):** `archive.session(id)` is called on the `PreToolUse` hold path before raising a held-push authority ask (`packages/hub/src/holds.ts`, bounded by `ARCHIVE_WAIT_MS = 2000`). It calls `await sources(options)`, which recursively `readdir`s every registered agent's entire transcript hierarchy across all projects and date folders before filtering `letters(source.session) === wanted`. When a session's `transcript_path` is already known to the hub or narrowed by session ID, walking thousands of historical transcripts on disk risks timing out `ARCHIVE_WAIT_MS` and leaving push targets unplaced (`unknown`) on the card.

**Design:** [One event log, with tables built from it](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#one-event-log-with-tables-built-from-it) · [Plans before acting](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#plans-before-acting)

### Scope
- Replace `Buyer.sync()`'s unfiltered `record.read` loop in `packages/buying/src/index.ts` with `readSince(this.o.record, this.cursor, ['card_rule.set'], ...)`
- Narrow `archive.session(id)` in `packages/archive/src/index.ts` (and its call from the hub) so copying one session's transcript checks a known path or matches the session's segment without walking unrelated session files when avoidable

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On a record holding 10,000 non-`card_rule.set` events after the last purchase, `buy()` reads only `card_rule.set` rows (`record.read` is called with `kinds: ['card_rule.set']`) and advances its cursor to the log head
- [ ] Copying a single active session via `archive.session(id)` with 2,000 unrelated transcript files in sibling project/date folders completes well within `ARCHIVE_WAIT_MS` and archives only the target session
- [ ] `tests/acceptance/69/`, `tests/acceptance/20/` and `tests/acceptance/1156/` pass unchanged

### Proof
Targeted unit tests on `@deepbuild/buying` (asserting `kinds` filter and cursor advance) and `@deepbuild/archive` (timing `session(id)` beside 2,000 sibling transcripts), before and after.

### Depends on
- none

`runProbe()` in `packages/conformance/src/probe.ts`, called by `packages/checks-numbers/src/run.ts` and `packages/checks-work/src/run.ts`, starts each probe with `spawn(process.execPath, [probe], { cwd: ctx.checkout, detached: true })` and sends `SIGKILL` to `-child.pid` at the deadline.

Found by reading `origin/main` at `145315636`. Unlike `@deepbuild/checks-command` (which starts, signals and waits for every check process through `host@1` so `@deepbuild/supervisor` confines it in Seatbelt or bubblewrap, tracks grandchildren that leave the process group by sandbox marker, and holds leases until every process is proven gone), `runProbe()` bypasses the supervisor:

- Probe processes run outside the platform sandbox.
- No `process.tracked` or `process.ended` events are recorded for the run.
- A child process spawned by a probe that detaches from the probe's process group (`setsid`) survives `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL')` on overrun.

**Design:** [Blocks for plug-ins that host something live](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#blocks-for-plug-ins-that-host-something-live) · [One hub per user, a tiny hook client, and extensions in-process](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#one-hub-per-user-a-tiny-hook-client-and-extensions-in-process)

### Scope
- Hub-bound check runners (`checks-numbers`, `checks-work`) receive `host@1` on their check context (as `ExtensionHost.checkContext` already comments for hub-bound check kinds) and start probes through `host@1` when present
- Standalone kit runs with no supervisor keep deterministic local probe execution only for kit fixtures, or run against a test host
- Probe overrun and cleanup prove every tracked process gone through the host before resolving

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When `checks-numbers` or `checks-work` runs through the extension host on a real supervisor, the probe starts through `host@1` and records `process.tracked` and `process.ended` in the event log
- [ ] A probe child that detaches into its own session and sleeps past the check's deadline is reaped by the supervisor's cleanup when the run ends `overran`
- [ ] `tests/acceptance/68/` and `tests/acceptance/87/` continue to pass

### Proof
A regression test with a real supervisor and extension host showing `process.tracked` / `process.ended` recorded and a detached child reaped on deadline, failing before and passing after.

### Depends on
- none

Seven defects in the 3D scene module and its renderer.

Found by the Nov 9 whole-project audit ([report](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/20f19f16c96650ce7c129b241479cbddc9d6380c/reports/whole-project-audit-2026-11-09.md); area file [`09-scene3d.md`](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/20f19f16c96650ce7c129b241479cbddc9d6380c/reports/whole-project-audit-2026-11-09/09-scene3d.md)). A second reader then tried to refute each finding against the code at `20f19f16`, the branch of PR #2113, and these held. They were read from the code, not reproduced, unless a line says so. Line numbers are on that branch.

**Epic:** #310 · **Design:** [Look `look@1`: print finishes](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#look-look1-print-finishes) · [Level of detail: proxies](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#level-of-detail-proxies) · [Material: texture maps](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#material-texture-maps)

### Scope
- Keep such documents off the fast path: `fast_path(map, &program, &scene).filter(|_| look.print.is_identity())`, and return `None` from `fast_path` when `scene.water.is_some()` or any layer has puffs. Faster, as a follow-up: recompute the print frame in the fast branch (it is `Copy`) and fold it into `changed`.
- Mix the ratio and the error into the hash passed to `levels` in `proxy_of`: `hash ^ 0x5052_4f58_5900_0000 ^ p.ratio.to_bits().rotate_left(17) ^ p.error.unwrap_or(-1.0).to_bits().rotate_left(41)`.
- Take the sign a file's TANGENT has, which the shader's formula and the import already assume: flip the box's `w` at :59 and its comment, set the caps' `w` to 1 at :90, and flip the test at :197. The other way round also works but then file tangents need their `w` negated at import.
- sets.rs:103: `if num(params.get("range")).is_none() {`.
- Before the insert, `if m.len() >= 64 { m.clear(); }`, as the crease store does.
- Return `std::borrow::Cow<'a, [u8]>` from `buffer`: borrowed for the binary chunk and a resolved external buffer, owned for a decoded data URI. Both callers only read the bytes.
- Delete `unit_ev100` with its doc comment, and the `use deep_canvas::ops;` line it leaves unused.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **The frame fast path moves everything in the scene that reads t.** Given the fast path test's document under a look with `print.grain.rate > 0`, when `Frames::at` and the whole evaluation are compared at five times past one grain step, then the two scenes are equal. Today they differ in `print` at every such time.
- [ ] **A proxy mesh's hash reads its ratio and error.** Given one mesh and hash, when `proxy_of` is called with ratio 0.5 and with ratio 0.25, then the two levels' hashes differ. Today they are equal.
- [ ] **Every mesh's tangents give the bitangent one sign.** Given the three unit meshes and a mesh with generated tangents, when `dot(cross(n, t) * w, dP/dv)` is taken over every triangle, then it has one sign everywhere. Today the box, the bottom cap and generated tangents give one sign, and the cylinder's side, its top cap and the sphere give the other.
- [ ] **A light with power from_file and range auto takes its range from the file's lumens.** Given a light with `power: from_file` and a 4,000 lm distribution, when it is read with `range: "auto"` and with no `range`, then the two ranges are equal. Today the first is the 800 lm range.
- [ ] **The proxy store is bounded.** Given 100 calls of `proxy_of` with 100 different hashes, when the store is counted, then it holds at most 64 entries. Today it holds 100.

- [ ] **The Linux sandbox's filter stops an x32 call on x86_64, so no call skips its rules.** Given the x86_64 lane, when a helper probe inside a run makes `syscall(0x40000000 | __NR_getpid)`, then the process dies by SIGSYS. Today the call returns (a PID, or ENOSYS on a kernel without x32).

### What goes wrong today
**The Linux sandbox makes each socket and metadata call it checks itself, so what was checked is what runs** (high; `packages/supervisor/native/helper-linux.c:724`, `packages/supervisor/native/helper-linux.c:691`, `packages/supervisor/native/helper-linux.c:776`; audit ID ts-small-a-16)

Read from the C only; not run on Linux. A program in a run with no host grant calls `connect(tcp_fd, p, 16)` with `*p` holding family AF_NETLINK while a second thread rewrites `*p` to an outside AF_INET address. The parent reads netlink and answers CONTINUE; the kernel copies `*p` again and connects outside, and no `sandbox.denied` is written. The same swap turns an AF_UNIX `bind` into a bind on any TCP port. A metadata change on a path the parent could not find is continued, so it can land on a file made in between, and `utimes`, `utime` and `futimesat` are continued after their check. Opens the parent allowed are continued too, so the refusal of `.claude/`, `.codex/` and `.mcp.json` holds only for a program that does not swap its path after the check.

`if (a.ss_family == AF_NETLINK) { CONTINUE(v); return; }` and `if (is_bind) { CONTINUE(v); return; }`, under the function's own comment "checked here, and made on the process's own socket, so what was checked is what connects". CONTINUE answers with `SECCOMP_USER_NOTIF_FLAG_CONTINUE`, which runs the call again from the program's memory. The design says each connect, bind, rename and metadata change is made "on the program's descriptor itself".

**The Linux sandbox's filter stops an x32 call on x86_64, so no call skips its rules** (high; `packages/supervisor/native/helper-linux.c:470`, `packages/supervisor/native/helper-linux.c:520`; audit ID ts-small-a-17)

Read from the C only; not run on Linux. On an x86_64 kernel built with the x32 ABI, a program calls `syscall(0x40000000 | __NR_socket, AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0)` and `syscall(0x40000000 | __NR_connect, ...)`. The filter sees arch AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64 and a number that equals none of its rules, falls to its last `RET(SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW)`, and the run opens any socket and connects anywhere. The `ptrace`, `io_uring` and `pidfd_getfd` refusals are skipped the same way. aarch64 is not affected.

`JEQ(ARCH_NR, 1, 0); RET(SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS); LD_NR;`, then every rule is `JEQ(nr, ...)` and the filter ends `RET(SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW);`. A grep of the file for `0x40000000` and `X32` finds nothing.

Read from the C only; not run on Linux. A run with no `listen` grant makes a TCP socket and calls `listen()` with no `bind()`. The kernel binds it to a free port on every address, so the run takes connections from the LAN on a port no grant named; the macOS profile allows inbound only on granted ports. On Linux 6.13 or later `setxattrat` and `removexattrat` also reach no rule, so a file's attributes outside the write grant can change.

The `notified` list starts `__NR_connect, __NR_bind` and holds the xattr calls by their old names only; it has no `__NR_listen`, and the filter ends `RET(SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW);`. packages/supervisor/src/types.ts says of `listen`: `"<host>:<port>" it may listen on`.

Note: Two more parts of this finding are the owner's call and are not in the issue above. Signals are scoped only on Landlock ABI 6 while the floor is ABI 4 and there is no PID namespace: raise the floor, or send the kill calls to the parent? `/var` and `/opt` are readable by every run: keep them, or name the subfolders programs need?

`const read = [repo, ...gitDirs(repo), dirname(dirname(dirname(git)))];` and `return process.platform === 'darwin' ? undefined : '/usr/bin/git';`; `node -e` gives `/` for that path. bubblewrap.ts passes each read path as `--read`, and the helper adds a Landlock read rule for it.

#266 gives a 2D piece a follow camera: a spring, a deadzone, a look-ahead and a shake in `camera.lib@1`. None of them knows where the level ends, so a follow that tracks a player to the left wall shows half a screen of nothing past it, and the piece passes every check, because `playtest.camera` measures only how much of the player is hidden and how close the camera sits to a solid. The design holds a viewer's own pan inside bounds (Shot: `user.pan`), but a logic shot turns the viewer's offsets off, so nothing holds a camera the rules drive. The fix every 2D game ends up writing by hand has two traps. Clamping only the centre leaves the view's edge outside. Clamping only what the spring returns leaves the spring's own state outside, so the camera sticks to the wall after the player has turned back. #266 is at 15 criteria, so this is its own task.

**Epic:** #187 · **Design:** [Camera and overlay](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#camera-and-overlay) · [Shot: poses from logic](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#shot-poses-from-logic) · [Logic: library interfaces](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#logic-library-interfaces) · [Check input: playtest](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#check-input-playtest)

**Runs on:** Spark: evaluated data, the library's fixtures and headless playtest runs; no GPU

### Scope
- `camera.lib@1` exports a 2D bounds clamp that takes `bounds: {x, y, w, h}` in u and the view's size. On an axis where the bounds are at least as wide as the view, the target is held to [min + half the view, max − half the view]. On an axis where the bounds are narrower than the view, the target is the centre of the bounds. The view's height is `view_width` × the frame's height ÷ its width
- The order in the reference library: the deadzone, then the clamp on the goal, then the follow spring, then the clamp again on what the spring returns. The second clamp doesn't change the spring's own state. A shake is added after both and may show up to its `max` past an edge
- The playtest's `camera` takes `inside: {x, y, w, h} | none = none` for a 2D shot. At every `every`-th step it reads the stored pose without the shake and fails the run with `playtest.camera`, naming the run, the step and the measure `inside`, when an edge of the view lies more than 1e-6 u outside the rectangle. An axis where the rectangle is narrower than the view passes while the view is centred on it within 1e-6 u
- The default: nothing is clamped or measured until a piece or a playtest gives a rectangle, because an open world has no edge. A playtest that names a 2D logic shot in `camera` and leaves `inside` out says so in one reading, `playtest.camera_unbounded`, naming the playtest; writing `inside: none` is the answer that quiets it
- Not in this task: a clamp on the ground plane in 3D, and bounds that aren't one rectangle (rooms, a polygon)

A piece can't leave the hub it was made on and stay a piece. #1790 lists everything a revision needs, and says that moving a document and its closure to another machine isn't in that task. `deep backup` (#572, closed) moves a whole record, with every event and all evidence, to restore one hub. The web player (#172) carries a document and its files to a browser, where it plays and can't be patched. So an agent that hands a scene to another person's hub copies layer files by hand, and the other hub finds on open that a pack version or a job's mesh is missing. This adds one archive that holds a revision and its closure and nothing else. The strong default needs no choice from the agent: the archive holds every entry the listing names, and opening it never fetches, never runs a job and never overwrites, and gives a document with the same hash.

**Epic:** #579 · **Design:** [Revision](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#revision) · [Carried state: the cache manifest](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#carried-state-the-cache-manifest) · [Pack: retired and missing](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#pack-retired-and-missing) · [Evidence](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#evidence)

**Runs on:** Spark for every criterion, since each reads hashes and evaluated data and no pixel; criterion 1 also writes its second archive on the reference Mac

### Scope
- Export gains the target `document`, one of the export module's own writers, outside `export.target@1` as the web player's is. It writes one file: the revision's layer files, its closure listing (#1790) and every listed entry once under its sha256, a pack version as its files. The same revision gives the same bytes on any machine: entries are in listing order, and the file holds no time, owner, path or host name
- The archive never holds a record event, evidence, a secret, a handle or a cache that evaluation can rebuild. An asset whose license is not shareable or is unknown makes the export BLOCKED with one ask naming the asset, as a shared export is today, and no file is written
- `deep open <file>` checks every entry against its hash before it writes any. It then stores the entries, the pack versions as retired versions where another version is installed (#1958), the listing and the layer files. It fetches nothing and runs no job. A document with the same ID at the same hash is left as it is and the reply is `already_current`. One with the same ID at another hash is refused, naming both hashes
- `document.archive` joins the core's check kinds: it opens the archive in a fresh store with the network denied and compares the revision hash, the listing and the evaluated outputs with the source's
- Not in this task: opening over a document held at another revision, merging two histories, live sync between hubs, and moving record events or evidence

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new fixture `archive.scene`, which is #1790's `closure.scene` at revision 2 with every asset under a shareable license, archives with its 19 entries. The archive written on Spark and the one written on the reference Mac, from stores in different folders with different modified times, are the same bytes, and the criterion is BLOCKED while only one machine has run. A planted writer that stores each file's modified time gives two different files and fails, naming the first byte that differs
- [ ] A fresh hub with no pack installed and the network denied opens the archive: the revision hash equals the source's, `document.closure` passes with 19 entries, every evaluated output and content key at 20 sampled times equals the source's, and the open makes 0 fetches and 0 job runs. A planted opener that leaves the stub job's mesh out and runs the job again fails, naming the job
- [ ] An archive with one byte flipped in its last entry is refused, naming the entry's role and hash, and the store holds 0 new blobs. One with an entry missing and one with a file the listing doesn't name are each refused, naming it. A planted opener that writes each entry before it checks the next leaves blobs behind and fails, naming the count
- [ ] With one asset marked `shareable: false`, and again with one asset's license left out, the export is BLOCKED with one ask naming that asset and writes 0 files. A planted writer that reads no license writes the archive and fails, naming the asset
- [ ] Opening the same archive a second time writes 0 blobs and 0 events and answers `already_current`. After one local patch to the opened document, the open is refused, naming both hashes, and the patched document is unchanged. A planted opener that overwrites it fails, naming the lost revision
- [ ] On a hub with a new fixture version `study@1.1.0` installed, the opened document still expands with `study@1.0.0`: every derived ID and the revision hash equal the source's. A planted opener that takes the installed version fails, naming the first ID that differs

- `{patch: ULID, doc, base: rev, writer (from the connection), reason: string, gesture: serial (optional), dry_run: bool = false, coalesce_key: string (optional), ops: [op]}`
- Ops: `create {item}`; `set {id, path, value}`; `unset {id, path}`; `delete {id, cascade = false}`; `move {id, parent, keep: world | local = world}`; `reorder {id, after | before}`; `rows {id, append | set | remove, by key}`; `break_out {instancer, element} | {instance, item}` (an instancer's element, or a recipe instance's derived item)
- Result: `{outcome: applied | superseded | conflict | refused, rev, ids: {~n → ID}, achieved: {created: {kind: n}, updated: n, deleted: {kind: n}, unchanged: bool}, issues: [{code, ids, path, actual, what, fix}], truncated: {shown, total, by_code}, cost_delta: {cpu_ms, gpu_ms, vertices, lights, gpu_mb}, undo: [op]}` (`undo`: the inverse ops, for the same writer; `truncated`: only when the issues were cut at the read cap, as What holds a document to its rules says)
- Refusal codes (closed): `not_your_layer, lease_held, derived_item, record_view, unknown_kind, kind_too_new, unknown_field, out_of_range, ref_unresolved, cycle, over_budget, stale_base, undo_conflict, gesture_required, too_large, over_quota, module_missing, pack_missing, unintended_removal, outside_selection, preview_unrequested`
- It can never: Edit a view of the record; apply in part; take its writer from the payload; target a derived item; undo another writer's change

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On a fixture film, moving a key 6 frames later, moving a stage marker to 2.5 s and setting a light's power, each one recorded gesture in the panel, gives the same patch ops, the same doc.patched entry apart from its writer and serial, and the same check result and issues as a test agent sending those ops to a twin of the film whose items are in its own layer; a planted panel that writes the document other than by patch, or adds or drops an op, fails, naming the edit
- [ ] Setting a key whose spring overshoots its channel's hard range, and dragging a shot's end past the next shot's start with no transition joining them, are each refused at commit: no presented frame shows the refused state, by the frame callbacks' revisions, the last good revision stays current, by hash, and the panel lists each edit with its issue's code and fix; during each drag the preview never shows a state whose dry run failed; and a planted panel that applies an edit and then reverts it fails, naming the frame that showed it
- [ ] You move two keys and set a value in the panel, then a test agent adds a marker and moves a key in its own layer; three undos in the panel remove exactly your three edits, one a step, leaving a document equal, by hash, to one where only the agent's edits were made; a planted undo that reverts the document's last patch whatever its writer fails, naming the agent's patch
- [ ] A recorded pen drag of a key from 1.00 s to 2.00 s whose release sample lies 3 px past the last move commits the ops of the last previewed dry run, 2.00 s, by hash; a planted panel that recomputes the value from the release sample commits 2.04 s and fails, naming the key

Some work can't land in one repo: an API change and the client that calls it, or a library and the app that pins it. Today the start card names one repo, and Send stays off without it (#574). A session gets one worktree (#575), and a stop's claim snapshots one worktree. A session that reaches into a second repo does it outside any worktree DeepBuild made, and nothing in the design says whether its claim sees those files.

**Epic:** #241 · **Design:** [Starting a session from the app](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#start) · [Sessions that know about each other](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#sessions-that-know-about-each-other) · [An agent says it's done](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#an-agent-says-its-done)

The session starts in the first repo's worktree and is given the others through the agent's own flag for extra folders, as its facts name it. An agent whose facts name none reads "one repo only" on the card, and a second repo can't be added
- A stop that did work makes one claim per repo the turn changed. Each is snapshotted and judged in its own temporary checkout (#31), against that repo's own approved checks. A scene draws only with every asset, pack version and job output its document names, and some of those are reached only through a material, a pack, or a pack another pack requires. Each store guards its own part today: `doc.patched` is the commit point for the document's layer files (#96, closed), #1410 syncs the evidence a FULL commit names, #203 keeps a pack version a document names, and #579 keeps a cache entry a revision names. Nothing lists the whole set a revision needs, so nothing proves that set is on disk when the revision is. A `doc.patched` event is a stream event, not a FULL commit, so #1410's rule doesn't reach the blobs a revision names, and the evidence store's 30-day retention (#15) has no rule that keeps an asset a current document names. This adds one listing per revision, one write order, one set of retention roots and one answer when an entry is gone.

**Epic:** #579 · **Design:** [Revision](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#revision) · [Carried state: the cache manifest](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#carried-state-the-cache-manifest) · [Pack: retired and missing](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#pack-retired-and-missing) · [Evidence](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#evidence)

**Runs on:** Spark for the listing, the crash suite under the test VFS, retention and the reopen, which read hashes and evaluated data; the reference Mac for the sync-recording shim, since only macOS has `F_FULLFSYNC`

### Scope
- `closure {doc, rev, entries: [{role, name, sha256, bytes}], count, bytes}`: one listing per revision of everything outside its own layer files that the revision needs to evaluate. An entry is an asset, a pack version by the digest of its files, a library, a program, a table, a job's output, or a document shown inside this one. What evaluation can rebuild is a cache and is not listed
- The listing follows every reference to its end: a material's `maps`, a pack's own assets, libraries, programs and tables, `requires.packs`, and a library's `needs`. An entry's identity is its role and its content, never a file name or a path
- The listing is written by hash and named by the revision's `doc.patched` event. A patch that changes no reference names the same listing and writes none
- Evaluation, checks and exports read a blob only through the revision's listing. `document.closure` joins the core's check kinds: a read of a hash the listing lacks FAILs it, naming the role and the hash, at whatever time the read happens
- Write order: every blob a revision adds, its layer files and its listing included, is synced with its folder before any record sync that can make its `doc.patched` event durable. An event that survives a power cut then never names a blob that didn't. A patch's reply and a hook call wait for no sync
- Retention roots: an entry stays while a current or pending revision, a save, a held checkpoint, a golden, a decision's evidence, or a revision an undo step can still return to lists it. The evidence store's retention pass (#15), the cache manifest (#579) and the pack store's count (#203) all read these roots, and a pack version reached only through `requires.packs` counts as named
- A listed entry whose bytes are gone or fail their hash is reported with its role, its hash and the path that reaches it, as `asset_missing` and `pack_missing` report theirs. Each check and export that needs it is BLOCKED until the same bytes are back, and nothing draws in its place. An entry the cache manifest holds follows the manifest's own rule
- A job output's entry also carries `made_from: [{name, sha256}]`: each input its `made_by` names, by asset ID and by the hash that asset had when the output entered the document
- `document.closure` raises `derived_stale {entry, input, was, now}` when the revision holds that asset under another hash. An output made from a stale output is stale too. The mark is worked out from the listing on every read and is never stored, so putting the first bytes back clears it
- Each check and export that needs a stale entry is BLOCKED until its job has run again and the new output has entered the document, as a missing entry blocks them. The patch's reply lists `stale: [{entry, job}]` in the order the jobs must run
- Not in this task: moving a document and its closure to another machine, any change to #157's all-or-nothing export, batching syncs past one per blob, and how long undo steps are kept, which decides how long the undo root holds

- [ ] `closure.scene` at revision 1 lists exactly 16 entries: 12 assets of 1 MiB each (8 that items name, 2 that only a material's `maps` name and 2 that only a pack names), 3 pack versions (study@1.0.0 and lamp@1.0.0, which the document lists, and shelf@1.2.0, reached only through study's `requires.packs`) and 1 mesh a stub job made. The assets' `bytes` sum to 12,582,912, and 3 blobs in the store that nothing names are not listed. A planted lister that follows no material, no pack's own entries and no `requires.packs` lists 11 and fails `document.closure`, naming the 5 it missed
- [ ] Dropping any one of the 16 entries from the listing fails `document.closure` over the fixture's span, naming that entry's role and hash, while every entry still listed reads back whole: 16 planted listings, 16 failures. Replacing one material map with a different valid image changes that entry's hash and no other entry, and moving the store to another folder changes 0 entries
- [ ] The crash suite runs its three passes (a power cut at each numbered write point, the Nth write failing for each N, and the last unsynced write torn) while a patch commits revision 2, which adds an asset an item names, a material map and a pack version. After every reopen either revision 2 is current and each of its 19 entries reads back whole, or revision 1 is current with its 16. A planted store that renames a blob into place without syncing it and its folder leaves revision 2 current without that blob after one cut and fails, naming the hash
- [ ] In those passes a patch whose blob write failed is never answered `applied`, and the sync-recording shim sees no sync between a patch's arrival and its reply. A patch that changes only values names the same listing hash as the revision before it. A planted writer that answers `applied` after its layer file's write failed fails, naming the patch, and one that syncs inside the reply fails, naming the sync
- [ ] With the test clock 31 days past the last write and shelf@1.2.0 uninstalled, the evidence store's retention pass and the pack store's sweep keep all 19 entries of revision 2 and remove the 3 blobs nothing names. A planted pass that keeps only what a decision or an archived transcript cites removes an asset and fails, naming its hash and the document. An extension holds things in the host while it runs: handlers, sources and their polls, schedules, actions, a panel, keymap chords and, when sandboxed, a process. The cleanup is proven one piece at a time: 20 enable and disable rounds leave no listener or callback (#350, closed), a failed mount keeps the old panel drawing (#360), two plug-ins on one chord are reported (#401, closed) and the supervisor proves a run's processes gone (#236). Nothing counts every kind of holding in one place, across several packages and orders, or after a failed update, a rollback and a hub restart. So a leftover timer or chord is found by a person, and a slot added later has no cleanup test at all. This adds a tally the host keeps and a kit part that compares it with its baseline after each of those moves.

**Epic:** #360 · **Design:** [Extension API (TypeScript, in-process)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#extension-api-typescript-in-process) · [Keymap, placement, window](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#keymap-placement-window) · [Panel](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#panel) · [Panel runtime and panel host](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#panel-runtime-and-panel-host)

**Runs on:** Any machine through the replica; no criterion reads a pixel or a wall clock.

### Scope
- The host keeps a tally by package and version: one count for each slot in the published contract's slot list (#349), and beside them the package's keymap chords, its schedules' pending timers, its calls under way, its leases and the processes under its run token. The host writes it, and no package reports its own
- The extension host's kit (#348) gains a lifecycle part. It reads the tally before a move and after it, and fails on any row that differs from the expected one, naming the package, the version and the slot
- The moves it runs: a load, an unload, unloads in another order, a second and a third load, an update that fails to mount, a rollback, and a hub stop and start
- Its fixture is three sandboxed test packages `a`, `b` and `c`. Each holds one `on` handler, one polled source, one schedule every minute, one action, one panel and one chord (⌥1, ⌥2 and ⌥3, each in its own panel): 6 rows and 1 process a package
- A slot in the contract's list with no count in the tally fails the kit, naming the slot
- A fourth fixture package `d` is a hub-bound release package that holds one environment and one lease: 1 row and 1 lease. Its environment's stop can be planted to reject or never to settle. It loads before `a`, `b` and `c`
- One more move: a hub stop in which one package's stop fails. A package whose stop throws or overruns its deadline doesn't end the stop. The host unloads every other package, releases the failing package's leases and removes its folder, and reports the failure once, naming the package and what didn't stop
- After the host's close the hub still closes the supervisor and the record and writes its `stopped` state, as `stop()` in `packages/hub/src/core.ts` does after a clean close. Seen on the Mac on 2026-11-06 during the #1119 perf-area run (R3): a `deep lease -- npx vitest …` whose vitest leader had crashed never returned. `runGroup` in `packages/hub/src/heavy.ts` waited for the whole process group to be gone (`while (groupAlive(child.pid)) await sleep(100)`) before resolving, so one stray child the leader left behind (a sleep, a worker, a browser) held `deep lease` and its slot for as long as it lived. The user's shell saw a hang; the hub kept the cpu slot held.

The slot's hold is the hub's job (#1015 AC4: held until the whole group ends, found by the hub tick's `groupAlive`), not the client's. The client should end when the command it ran ends, with that command's exit code, and tell the hub so; the hub keeps the lease while the group runs on and returns it once the tick finds the group gone.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `deep lease -- <cmd>` returns within a second of `<cmd>` exiting, with `<cmd>`'s exit code, even when `<cmd>` left a child running: `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 300 & echo $!; exit 3'` returns 3 at once, the sleep still running.
2. With a hub up, the cpu slot the lease held is not released while the leftover child lives, and is released within 5 s of that child ending: the hub's tick, not the client, returns it.
3. The same holds with no hub (an empty HOME) and on the `DEEP_LEASED` path: the client returns when the leader exits.

Expected values: exit code 3; return under 5000 ms; `lease.acquired` once; `lease.released` absent while the child lives and present within 5 s of its SIGKILL.

Codex can run every session in one background server that updates itself. An update restarts that server, which can cut off a running turn. The new server resumes the thread and starts a turn of its own with a hidden message to continue. DeepBuild's facts know that shape for goals but not for this, so the new turn's origin reads unknown. No recorded session covers a restart, so nothing shows the session stays one session across it. Claude Code runs background sessions under a daemon of its own, and the facts don't cover that either.

- The session is bound to the new server by its resume start, and stays one row

A lead session often hands its work to children defined in the repo's `.claude/agents/*.md`. Each has a role, its own tools and often its own model: a designer, a programmer pinned to a cheaper model, a tester. The record keeps only `{parent, child, task_ref}` for each child, and review rules read "the model that made a change" from the lead's transcript. So code written by a child on one model is credited to the lead's model, and a review by that same model counts when it shouldn't. A lead's instruction to "write your output to `<path>`" is also not checked. A child can stop with a fluent reply and no file. Keep each child's role and model in the record, and hold a child to the file its lead names.

**Epic:** #6 · **Design:** [What each agent gives us, and the limits we design around](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#what-each-agent-gives-us-and-the-limits-we-design-around) · [Hook protocol (deep-hook and the hub)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#hook-protocol-deep-hook-and-the-hub) · [Sessions that know about each other](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#sessions-that-know-about-each-other)

### Scope
- `session.child_started` gains `agent_type`, the sha256 of the agent definition file at the child's start (when the agent has one), and the model read from the child's own transcript. A child whose transcript names no model reads `model: unknown`
- Changes are credited to the child that wrote them, by its Write and Edit calls. Review rules (#87) and the picker's past results (#117) read the child's model and definition digest
- Setup lists, as a reading, each agent definition whose `tools:` allowlist leaves out DeepBuild's MCP tools. Its children are still held at their stop until their checks pass (#90)
- A lead's first prompt to a child that names an output file (`Write your full output to <path>`) adds a requirement on that child. The file must exist, be non-empty, and be written during the child's span. Placeholders and quoted text add none

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On a recorded Claude Code session on an Opus model whose diff lines are all written by a child started as `programmer` with `model: sonnet`, `session.child_started` carries `agent_type: programmer`, the definition's digest and a Sonnet model from the child's transcript. A reader that copies the lead's model fails, naming the child
- [ ] There, a #87 review answered by a Sonnet model is uncounted with the reason "review by the model that made the change: child <id>", and an Opus review counts. A diff written by two children on two models lists both; a review by either is uncounted for that child's lines. A child with `model: unknown` makes its lines' reviews uncounted, never counted
- [ ] After `.claude/agents/tester.md` changes between two runs, the two children show two digests. The picker's reading of them is #117's
- [ ] A child whose first prompt ends "Write your full output to `production/qa/plan.md`" and which stops without writing it is held at its stop with one send-back naming the path, and its claim is never PASS. A reply saying "Written to production/qa/plan.md" with no file is held the same way. A file that existed before the child started, unchanged by digest, doesn't meet the requirement
- [ ] `<path>`, `[path]` and `{path}` add no requirement, and neither does the phrase inside a file the child read. A reader that scans the whole transcript adds one from a Read result and fails, naming the quote. The lead's stop is held until every child's named file exists

### Proof
The recorded sessions with each child's start event, digest and model; the credited changes; the counted and uncounted reviews; and the held children with their named files.

"all done?" typed in a real Claude Code session is never answered from the record: the prompt hook can't tell it's yours, so it goes to the model.

**Epic:** #3 · **Design:** [The verdict in the chat](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#an-agent-says-its-done): "A message typed into the session that only asks for status, such as "still going?" or "all done?", is answered from the record by the prompt hook, without waking the model."

### What happens
- The status answer (#83, #669) blocks the prompt only when the prompt's origin is `person`. The origin joins the hook's `prompt_id` to the prompt's transcript entry (`turnOrigin: human`).
- Claude Code 2.1.308 writes a typed prompt's transcript entry only once its `UserPromptSubmit` hooks have returned. Measured in #567: 154 ms after a quick hook fired, 3,166 ms after a hook that sleeps 3 s. Its payload carries no origin of its own (`cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `permission_mode`, `prompt`, `prompt_id`, `scratchpad_dir`, `session_id`, `transcript_path`).
- So at the prompt hook, a status question you type in a real session has no origin. `statusReply` reads it as not yours, and the question goes to the model. #567 (PR #1262) fixed the same gap for recording prompts by placing them after the hook. A status answer can't wait like that: it has to block the prompt at its hook.
- #669's fast tests pass only because their Claude Code stand-in writes the entry before it fires the hook. Its live file, which checks this criterion, has never run (PR #1221: no token or covered version was on the Mac).

### Scope
- Read a Claude Code status question whose entry isn't written yet as yours, unless the session's transcript already shows it came in as an automatic prompt (a task notice, another session's or agent's message: the queue's automatic entries, `AUTOMATIC_QUEUED`). Record the prompt it blocked as yours.
- No change for a prompt whose entry is already there, or for Codex and pi.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In a real Claude Code session, "all done?" typed after a verdict is answered from the record by DeepBuild's prompt entry, blocking the prompt so no model call is made (#669's live AC5, `tests/acceptance/669/session.live.test.ts`, passes)
- [ ] The blocked prompt is recorded as yours (`user.ask` from `person`), and a status question that came in as an automatic prompt is not answered from the record
- [ ] #669's fast suite and #83's status tests still pass
- [ ] Claude Code's facts record, for the pinned version, whether a scheduled task's prompt (a `/loop` tick) has its transcript entry written before or after its `UserPromptSubmit` hooks. A scheduled "all done?" reaches the model unchanged and is never recorded as yours, as #83 requires; a fix that reads every prompt with no entry yet as yours answers it from the record when its entry comes later, and fails, naming the prompt

### Proof

A live 3D airport made by Claude Code and run end to end. A fictional regional field stands on its own layout and terrain: aircraft land, taxi on the centre lines, turn around at their stands and push back, every number on screen computed from the running model. A viewer clicks an aircraft and rides along with it, steps through the turnaround's stages, and changes the speed. The approach opens as a space-time cube where one light aircraft is too close behind a heavy one; dragging its tube clears the breach, and the readouts prove it. The terminal is built from its plan sheet and checked against the drawing's ink. The airport also has a survey look of dots over the land, and the hero airliner leaves as showcase stills in a world drawn as glyphs. Finally the same piece sits inside a team's own ops page, fed by that team's replayed feed through a field map. The host page's list selects in the view and the view's clicks open the host's panel. When the feed stops, the view says so and keeps its last state, and it recovers when the feed returns. The agent writes the piece, the app plays it, and the checks pass it on evaluated data.

A floor plan on paper is the most common record of a building, and a 3D house built from one is only right if its walls land on the drawing's lines. The building module (#420) builds walls, openings, slabs and roofs from numbers, but nothing reads those numbers off a plan sheet at its printed scale or checks the build against the drawing, so an agent's read of a plan is its word alone: a wall 30 cm off or a door on the wrong side passes. Add `plan.sheet`, a plan drawing kept as an asset with its scale calibrated from a printed dimension, and `plan.overlay`, a check that lays the built walls back over the drawing's ink, on the plan and on a section cut through the built house, and fails a build that doesn't land on it.

**Epic:** #310 · **Design:** [Building module](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#building-module) · [Asset job: imports](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#asset-job-imports) · [Check input: asset kinds](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#check-input-asset-kinds) · [Geometry audit: scenes](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#geometry-audit-scenes) · [Units and axes](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#units-and-axes)

**Runs on:** Any machine; the overlay is computed on the sheet's pixels and the building's evaluated geometry. Screenshots on the reference Mac.

### Scope
- `plan.sheet {image: asset (PNG, or a PDF page rendered at a set dpi), license, calibrate: {a: [px, px], b: [px, px], length: m} | {bar: [[px, px], [px, px]], length: m}, origin: [px, px], level: ID}`: the sheet's scale comes from one printed dimension or a scale bar, never from a guessed dpi.
- Ink: the check thresholds the sheet's luminance at `ink_below` into an ink mask, and the distance from every pixel to the nearest ink in metres at the sheet's scale.
- `plan.overlay {sheet, items: [ID], section_height: m = 1.2, tolerance: m = 0.07, share_min: 0..1 = 0.7, offset_max: m = 0.16, control_shift: m = 0.5}`: the check samples every built wall face of the named items along its length in plan, measured twice: from the walls' declared lines, and from a section cut through the building's evaluated geometry at `section_height`, mitres and openings included. Each pass finds the best-fit shift of the samples over the ink within `offset_max`, reads the share of samples within `tolerance` of ink, and does the same for the samples shifted by `control_shift` in eight directions. A pass needs a share of at least `share_min`, a fit no farther than `offset_max`, and a share at least 0.2 above the best control's, so a build that lands on any dense hatch can't pass.
- An opening is checked the same way: its jambs' samples against the ink of the gap in the wall.
- Values the drawing doesn't give, such as ceiling height, sill height or the roof's form, carry the `inferred` certainty mark (#1216) and are listed with the check's result.
- Thresholds are the check's own; a brief may tighten them, never loosen them.

### Fields
**[Building module](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#building-module)**
- `plan.sheet {image, license, calibrate, origin, level, ink_below: 0..1 = 0.5}`
- Check `plan.overlay {sheet, items, section_height, tolerance, share_min, offset_max, control_shift}` with results `{pass: plan | section, share, offset: [m, m], control_share, worst: [{item, at: m, distance: m}]}`
- It can never: Take its scale from the image's dpi; loosen a threshold for the working agent; pass a build its section fails; mark a value documented that the sheet doesn't show

A monitor of the world reads hundreds of news feeds in several languages. What a person needs from them is not 2,000 headlines but a few stories: which items tell the same story, how many separate outlets carry it, whether it is new or fading, where it happens, and a short brief whose every sentence you can trace to the items behind it. DeepBuild's sources turn numbers into readings, and free text stays an outside value shown with its source and age (#261), but nothing reads a feed, groups items into stories or tags them with places. Add a feed source kind and three steps after it: stories by text similarity, places by matching names a piece's map holds, and briefs and translations by runner jobs whose sentences each cite story rows.

**Epic:** #6 · **Design:** [Blocks for plug-ins that do real work](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#blocks-for-plug-ins-that-do-real-work) · [Honest numbers](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#honest-numbers) · [Bound value](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#bound-value) · [Salience `salience@1`](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#salience-salience1) · [Control: picks on rows and grid focus](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#control-picks-on-rows-and-grid-focus)

**Runs on:** Any machine for feeds, stories and places, against local test servers on a test clock; the runner criteria run headless in Claude Code.

### Scope
- Feed source: `feed {url}` polls RSS 2.0, Atom 1.0 or JSON Feed 1.1 with conditional requests (ETag and Last-Modified), within the source's quota, timeout and cadence. Each item becomes a row of `feed.item@1`: `{id, source, link, title, published, lang, summary}`, where `id` is the item's guid or, without one, the hash of its normalized link. Title and summary are outside text (#261): shown with source and age, cited by no check, verdict or notice. A feed that answers 304 makes no new rows; an item seen before is never a new row, even if its feed reorders.
- Sources: a plug-in's store may give each feed's publisher a `tier` (its own data, shown as a badge). Two feeds of one publisher count as one outlet.
- Stories: `stories {items, window: h = 48, threshold: f32 = 0.5}` groups items whose normalized title shingles (word 2-grams after case folding, script folding and stop words for the item's language) reach Jaccard similarity `threshold`, computed exactly by MinHash candidates checked in full. A story's key is its earliest item's ID, so it keeps its key as items join. It carries `items`, `outlets` (distinct publishers), `first_seen`, `last_seen` and `phase`: `breaking` while first seen in the last 2 h, `developing` while items keep arriving, `sustained` past 24 h with items in the last 6 h, `fading` after 6 h without one. Stories are a pure function of the recorded items, so a replay groups the same.
- Places: `places {items, shapes: geo.shapes@1, names: columns, aliases: columns}` tags an item with each region whose name or alias appears in its title as a whole word in the item's language, through the match transform's folding (#900), and keeps the matched byte span. A name the alias table marks `ambiguous` tags only when the same title also names the region's capital or another of its places the table lists. A tag is only ever a match a person can see in the title; no model guesses a place. An item whose title names no region has no place, and a story's places are the union of its items' with counts.
- Translation: a runner job `translate {item, to}` writes a translated title as a new outside value marked `translated_from: {item, lang}`. The original stays the item's title, both are shown, and place tags read only the original.
- Briefs: a runner job `brief {stories, sentences: ≤ 8}` returns sentences, each with the story keys it rests on. The hub refuses a sentence that cites no story or a story not in the job's input, counts the refused ones, and keeps the brief's as-of time as its oldest cited story's `last_seen`. A brief is a reading of outside text: shown with its sources and age, never a verdict. Picking a sentence picks its stories and their places, so a map can fly to them.
- A story list is a salience view: about nine stories a level, the rest folded into a count, ranked by a score the piece writes from `outlets`, phase and recency, never by the brief.

### Fields
**Source (amended)**
- `feed {url, formats: rss | atom | json_feed}` (a source kind); row layout `feed.item@1 {id: str ≤ 256, source, link, title, published: time | none, lang: BCP 47, summary}`
- Transforms: `stories {items, window, threshold}` → rows `{key, items, outlets, first_seen, last_seen, phase}`; `places {items, shapes, names, aliases (with `ambiguous` and `confirm_by` columns)}` → tags `{item, region, span: [start, end]}`
- Runner jobs: `translate {item, to}` → `{text, translated_from}`; `brief {stories, sentences}` → `[{text, cites: [story key]}]`
- Issues: `brief.uncited {job, sentence}`, `feed.refused {source, item, cause}`
- It can never: Count one item twice or one publisher twice; tag a place that isn't a visible match in the original title; let a brief sentence stand without a citation; rank stories by a model's opinion; treat text as a reading a check can cite

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Forty local feeds (RSS, Atom and JSON Feed) on a test clock publish 2,400 items over 26 h, written for this test in English, Spanish and Arabic; polling every 5 min records each item once, a 304 adds nothing, and a feed that reorders its items adds no rows; a planted reader that keys items by position fails, naming the duplicates
- [ ] The fixture holds 120 stories by construction; `stories` groups the items into exactly those 120, with each story's `outlets` equal to its distinct publishers (two feeds of one publisher count once) and its phase at hour 26 equal to the fixture's; a replay of the recorded items gives the same keys
- [ ] `places` over an admin-0 shapes asset with English, Spanish and Arabic names and aliases tags "Floods hit Valencia region" with no country, "Inundaciones en España" with Spain at the span of "España", and an Arabic title with Egypt at its name's span; "Jordan" is marked ambiguous in the alias table, so the fixture's 30 sports items that name only "Jordan" tag nothing and "Jordan reopens border crossing near Amman" tags Jordan at both spans; a planted tagger that matches substrings tags "Oman" inside "Romania" and fails, naming the item
- [ ] A `translate` job's output is shown beside the original with `translated_from`, and changing it changes no place tag
- [ ] A `brief` over the top 9 stories returns sentences each citing at least one of them; a recorded job answer with one uncited sentence and one citing a story outside its input shows the brief without both and records `brief.uncited` twice; the brief's age equals its oldest cited story's
- [ ] Picking a brief sentence picks its stories and the regions they're tagged with, and a map binding the pick flies to their bounds
- [ ] The story list shows nine stories and a "+111 more" fold, ranked by the piece's score; a planted ranking by brief order fails, naming the story
- [ ] Budgets, on the reference Mac in the local preflight, compared with the merge base: forty feeds polled and 2,400 items grouped and tagged in under 400 ms of hub CPU a poll, with stories updated in the app within 1 s of the poll
- [ ] Shown to you: screenshots of the story list, a story's items with their outlets, tiers and place spans highlighted, a translated title beside its original, and a brief with its citations, taken by the check run from the app, are attached to the PR and shown to you in the session. Whether they look right is one taste call, recorded; without it the run stays INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS, and no criterion above reads a picture to judge it

### Proof
The feed fixtures on a test clock with their row counts, the 120 constructed stories and their phases, the place tags with their spans in three languages, recorded runner answers for translation and briefs with the refusals, the pick-to-map run, and the budget runs beside the merge base. Planted wrong programs that must fail: items keyed by position, a substring tagger, an uncited sentence kept, stories ranked by the brief.

### Not in this task
Reading article pages beyond the feed's own fields; social networks and chat channels as sources; grouping by embeddings or a model; deciding whether a story is true; sending a brief anywhere, which is a send.
