The Map's zoom says a database opens into its tables and a service into the steps a request takes, but the map reads only workspaces, packages, folders and the tree-sitter repo map, so nothing says what a part holds. Read it from what the repo already declares, with no model, as the map's facts layer on `map.layer@1` (#259): every child cites its file and line, and a level nothing describes reads not known. An outside code wiki may add a summary to a row, never a row.

**Epic:** #6 · **Design:** [First-party extensions that ship on by default](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#first-party-extensions-that-ship-on-by-default) · [Blocks for plug-ins that host something live](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#blocks-for-plug-ins-that-host-something-live) · [A map beyond code](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#a-map-beyond-code)

### Scope
- Tables and their columns from schema files, migrations and model definitions; endpoints from API description files (OpenAPI, GraphQL schemas and protobuf) and from routes that tree-sitter queries find, each under the service whose build context holds the file that declares it, and one endpoint where an API description and a route share its method and path, with path parameters compared by position whatever their form; services and ports from compose and manifest files; calls between symbols from the repo map, marked approximate
- Each fact cites its file and line and is a row of the map's facts layer; readers for a language or a framework fill `repo.facts@1` through `deep.registerFacts`, many fills, and run out of process with read access to the repo only
- The `repo.facts@1` kit is a fixture repo per reader with the expected facts by file and line, and its planted fill reports a route at a line that holds none; the fact kinds (table, column, endpoint, handler, step, service, port and call) are a closed registry
- The receiver (#42) takes a journey run's service spans: env-local (#36) sets the service's OpenTelemetry endpoint to the receiver and adds the run's ID as a resource attribute, a value that grants nothing and is not the run token; those spans skip the agent fold and go into the run's evidence as one file, scrubbed as other evidence is, and a span with no known run ID belongs to no run
- With spans, a service's request steps come from that file, each step's file and line from the span's code attributes or else from the handler the repo map finds for its route, marked so; without them, an endpoint opens into its handler and the calls the repo map finds, marked static
- Files stay one view among these; a level nothing in the repo describes reads not known, never a guess; the map makes no model call and reads again only the files a change touched

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A part holding only `src/orders.ts` and `src/users.ts`, with no schema, API description, route or manifest, opens into its files and symbols, labelled as files, and its tables level reads not known; a planted reader that reports tables `orders` and `users` from those names fails the kit, naming `orders`
- [ ] A test plug-in's reader for one more route style, registered through `deep.registerFacts`, passes the `repo.facts@1` kit on its fixture of two routes, each with its file and line; a planted reader that reports a route at line 12 of a file whose line 12 holds none fails the kit, naming that file and line
- [ ] The `repo.facts@1` kit holds one fixture per source the scope names (a schema file, a migration folder, a model definition, an OpenAPI file, a GraphQL schema, a protobuf file, a router, a compose file and a manifest); the first-party readers pass each, and calls from the repo map show marked approximate
- [ ] A planted reader that writes a file into the fixture repo, or connects to `cdn.other.example`, is stopped by the platform sandbox with a `capability.refused` event naming the path or host, and none of its facts show; a host that runs readers in the hub's process lets the write land and fails, naming the file
- [ ] A journey run on the fixture service, with its spans sent to the receiver for the run, opens `POST /orders` into its 4 recorded spans; the 3 that carry code attributes show their file and line, the fourth shows its handler's file and line from the repo map, marked so, and each shows the check that ran it; with no spans, it opens into its handler and the calls the repo map finds, marked static; a view that shows static steps as recorded fails, naming the step
- [ ] During that run, a second process sends 3 spans for `POST /orders` to the receiver without the run's ID: the run's steps stay the 4 recorded ones and no run lists the 3; a receiver that files spans by time window alone shows 7 steps and fails, naming the spans
- [ ] A span whose `url.full` carries the run's injected `API_TOKEN` value `k3yZ9` is stored with it scrubbed in every form #15 names; a receiver that writes service spans without the run's scrub list fails, naming the span

A plug-in can draw on the Map today only as an agent's drawing, on a layer apart from the parts. A repo you fly into, or a live picture of your services, needs rows the map treats as its own: placed with the parts, opened level by level, bound to readings and kept in the record. Add one hub slot, `map.layer@1`, that the map's own facts layer (#260), the infra map (#72), the feature map and, later, the code-graph reader fill too. The slot is a fill under the composition rules, and a layer can't add a row that nothing supports. The record gains one event kind, `layer.rows`, and its projection, because the time scrubber, compare and detached handles must read rows as they were, and only the record pins them to a log position.

**Epic:** #6 · **Design:** [A map beyond code](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#a-map-beyond-code) · [Blocks for plug-ins that host something live](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#blocks-for-plug-ins-that-host-something-live) · [Composition](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#composition) · [Extension API (TypeScript, in-process)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#extension-api-typescript-in-process)

### Scope
- `deep.registerLayer(name, layer)` fills `map.layer@1`, many fills, with its kit and planted fills in the conformance package: `rows(project)` returns rows and links, and `children(id, level)` returns a row's children when that level is reached, never at load
- A row has a kind, a parent and a level, and anchors to a stable name the map already has or declares its own, prefixed with the layer's name. Its citation must name it: a record entry or a state source's item whose name is its anchor, a repo file and line at a commit that holds its name, or a measured reading whose series is keyed by its name without the layer's prefix. A model job's answer and an outside reading never support a row, and a row whose citation is missing or names something else is refused with the layer's code `unsupported`, naming the row and the citation
- The hub calls `rows` at start and whenever a record entry or state source item its rows cite is added or removed, or a series they cite gains or loses a key; a cited value that only changes redraws what is bound to it and never calls the layer. It records each result that differs, and each `children` answer, as one `layer.rows` event with the rows in one evidence file by hash, so the time scrubber, compare and detached handles read rows as they were
- A source's arguments may name `{row}`, the anchor of the row it is bound to; each row's call counts against the quota, rows the quota can't serve in a run make no reading and go first in the next, and the cache keys on the arguments
- A row's kind names a recipe by `name@version` from an installed pack for its open level; a kind with none, or whose named recipe isn't installed yet, draws as a graph of its children
- Size, height, color and a link's traffic bind to readings as bound values, in the layer's own colors kept at the look's distance from the status colors; a row whose paint breaks that is refused when the layer returns it; a lens sets color and height on its rows as on parts; the same rows draw in the 2D map and the 3D city, with no logic module and no code per frame
- A layer can't move, hide or restyle another layer's rows; filters, the scrubber, compare, ⌘K once a level has been reached, and point-and-ask work on its rows as on parts

### Scope
- Turn view: on every return, whatever the agent drew, a still `view` document the record writer builds from the returns projection, in the core view class: the turn's parts, changed ones first and read or fetched ones only while fewer than nine changed, at most nine by salience@1 (#394) with the rest folded into a count, in boxes by the Map's top-level parts and ordered by path, each with status-bound chips for the checks whose paths cover it and a changed part no check covers marked as a gap; under them a timeline from the record (#396) from the turn's prompt to its stop, fit to the card's width; a part opens the Map and a station the session's line; it reads no transcript text, and an agent's patch to it is refused with `not_your_layer`
- Its parts are selectable like the Map's: point and ask (#384) on a part sends that part's handle, its stable name, with the turn view's revision, so you can ask about exactly what a turn changed
- Parts: the returns projection gains `parts`, the paths of the turn's `tool.after` events, changed for an edit or a write, read for a read or a search, and fetched, by host only, for a fetch
- On the return card (#145) it draws after what needs you and before the proof, above anything the agent drew, so on a return with no ask it sits right under the verdict line; a return folded to one line keeps the turn view's line at line height beside it; and on an answer it shows what the turn read
- Its planted views join `return.card@1` (#145): a view that replaces the return card must show the turn view on every return, built from the record, or it fails the kit at install
- With the rest of the return card, it answers what a person asks on coming back: what changed and where, whether each requirement is proven, and what's left for you
- The turn view says whether its changed parts are complete or partial, and when partial, why, from a closed list: a shell command wrote files no hook reported, a change outside the worktree, a file too large or binary to read, a sensitive file left out, another session's turn in the same worktree overlapped this one (from the session map), or the turn failed. A partial turn view never reads as the whole change
- Under #1453: an opened card shows the turn view as one line, its changed parts counted with their worst state, and the boxes open from it. A folded return stays one row, with its turn's line in the row's accessible name

**Epic:** #310 · **Design:** [Patch](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#patch) · [Writer layer](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#writer-layer) · [Scope and input classes](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#scope-and-input-classes) · [Input router, focus and gesture serial](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#input-router-focus-and-gesture-serial) · [Editor panel: patches as you](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#editor-panel-patches-as-you) · [Selection (session state)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#selection-session-state)

### Scope
- Patches as the multi-writer task defines them (#96), results and refusal codes included; this task adds their dry run, which reports what a patch would achieve and any refusal codes, and the preview, snapping and gestures below
- A preview, kept as session state; snapping, guides and gestures that each produce one patch
- Kind rules that warn on the preview while you edit, and refuse your patch at commit as they refuse an agent's
- One interaction scope with its targeting and overlay rules, snap profiles per kind, and a preview that never rebuilds
- Your patch to another writer's item: where no live lease of that writer covers it, a patch from you that changes an item in its layer first takes the item into your layer with its ID and values, as a break-out does; its history records the take, that writer's later patches to it are refused with not_your_layer, and undoing the patch that took it hands it back as it was, so you can fine-tune what an agent made
- Patches from a panel: a panel's patch writes as you only from the editor panel the app ships, or from a panel whose plug-in you granted edit_as_you by name on its install card, which no agent can grant, and only when its gesture is the serial of your input that ended a gesture in that panel, from hardware input or VoiceOver, unspent, for the document open there; from such a panel one whose gesture fails this is refused with gesture_required and one without a gesture writes as the panel's plug-in, and every other panel's patch writes as its plug-in whatever its gesture, so a panel's own script, a timer, an agent's computer use, a replica or an agent-built panel's button can't write as you; the editor panel (its own task) writes only this way
- Selection as the agent's write boundary: a point and ask (#384) on a work product opens a shared lease for its ask-task on exactly the selected IDs and the items derived from them; the agent's patches to that document outside it are refused with `outside_selection`, naming the items, and inside it show only as a preview or up to three options (Variant) until you accept one with your gesture, which ends the lease and applies it as one patch written as you, one undo step; a `region` alone selects nothing, so it can be asked about but never patched
- Suggestions and put back: a patch whose only refusal is `not_your_layer` is filed as a suggestion on each of your items it touched, applied only by your gesture as one patch written as you, superseded by any later change to the item, and never an ask, recorded as `suggestion.filed` and `suggestion.settled`, which feed the `suggestions` projection the return card and the editor panel read; "Put back as before this stop", the return card's action, is one patch per document the agent's turn changed, written as you and shown first as a dry run, that gives each item back its values from before the turn's first change to it, creates its deleted items again with their IDs and deletes the ones it created, leaving out with `undo_conflict` what another writer changed since and with `lease_held` what a live lease covers; every item it puts back becomes yours
- A gesture that changes nothing commits nothing: a patch whose result is `unchanged` writes no `doc.patched`, no revision and no undo step, and a drag ended by Esc or by losing pointer capture commits nothing
- A write that has no effect says so: a `set` that leaves the item's built output and evaluated values the same, such as a param the item's current mode ignores, still applies and returns the issue `no_effect {id, path}`, so an agent never takes an unchanged result for a change
- A press on a member of a multi-selection keeps the set, and a plain click with no drag narrows to that item on release.

### Fields
**[Patch](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#patch)**
- `{patch: ULID, doc, base: rev, writer (from the connection), reason: string, gesture: serial (optional), dry_run: bool = false, coalesce_key: string (optional), ops: [op]}`
- Ops: `create {item}`; `set {id, path, value}`; `unset {id, path}`; `delete {id, cascade = false}`; `move {id, parent, keep: world | local = world}`; `reorder {id, after | before}`; `rows {id, append | set | remove, by key}`; `break_out {instancer, element} | {instance, item}` (an instancer's element, or a recipe instance's derived item)
- Result: `{outcome: applied | superseded | conflict | refused, rev, ids: {~n → ID}, achieved: {created: {kind: n}, updated: n, deleted: {kind: n}, unchanged: bool}, issues: [{code, ids, path, actual, what, fix}], truncated: {shown, total, by_code}, cost_delta: {cpu_ms, gpu_ms, vertices, lights, gpu_mb}, undo: [op]}` (`undo`: the inverse ops, for the same writer; `truncated`: only when the issues were cut at the read cap, as What holds a document to its rules says)
- Refusal codes (closed): `not_your_layer, lease_held, derived_item, record_view, unknown_kind, kind_too_new, unknown_field, out_of_range, ref_unresolved, cycle, over_budget, stale_base, undo_conflict, gesture_required, too_large, over_quota, module_missing, pack_missing, unintended_removal, outside_selection, preview_unrequested`

### Scope

- Each child's stop held until its checks pass; a send-back reaches that child as its next instruction
- The lead's stop held until every task is proven, every child has stopped, every worktree has an owner and every message you sent during the plan is linked to a task

### Fields
**[Event](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#event)**
- The only state the kernel keeps: `{id, kind, subject, writer, actor, scope, data, ts}`, with the writer taken from the connection and the actor and scope from its credential, and a `log_pos`, its position in the event log, that the hub assigns at append. Its kinds include these shapes:
  - `user.ask`, for each prompt and each message typed while the agent works;
  - `session.child_started`;
  - `claim.made`, with its scope: a session, a child or a task;
  - `task.created`;
  - `worktree.created` and `worktree.removed`;
  - `doc.patched`.
  Only the core appends the kinds that record a decision: `verdict.made` and `verdict.stale` from its verdict engine, `definition.locked` and `definition.revised` from its definition lock, and `decision.created`, `decision.applied`, `ask.answered` and `ask.defaulted` from the trusted path, its check of a resolver's answer and an ask's deadline. `deep.record.append` refuses each of them from every other writer, a first-party extension in the hub included, naming the kind, and the extension host's kit holds a planted first-party extension that tries.
- It can never: Carry a writer it claims rather than one its connection proves, or a `log_pos` the hub didn't assign; or record a verdict, a locked definition, a decision or an answer from any writer but the core

**[Attempt and plan](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#attempt-and-plan)**
- An attempt is one run at a task: `{task_ref, attempt, session or child, worktree, base}`. A plan is a projection of a lead's tasks and child sessions. The lead's stop is held until:
  - every task is proven;
  - every child session has stopped;
  - every worktree has an owner;
  - every message you sent during the plan is linked to a task.
- It can never: Deliver an answer or a send-back to a replaced attempt, or settle a merge while a child still holds leases on its paths

Turn runs into one honest verdict.

**Epic:** #3 · **Design:** [How runs become one of five verdicts](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#how-runs-become-one-of-five-verdicts) · [What done means, fixed at the start](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#what-done-means-fixed-at-the-start)

### Scope
- Precedence: FAIL, INVALID, BLOCKED, INCONCLUSIVE, PASS; every non-PASS result becomes an open item
- Runs needed: n = ceil(ln 0.05 / ln(1 − p)) for an accepted failure rate p
- Known failures match exact error text, with an owner and an end date or the condition that ends it, such as an upstream fix landing
- A verdict covers one commit; a new commit marks it stale
- A check that never starts on a claim's snapshot, because a quick check of the snapshot failed or was INVALID, its stop's reply kept the agent working, or a newer claim changed the check's inputs first (#29), stays pending on that claim with no run: the claim never passes on it, it is never read as a check that ran nothing, and nothing waits on it
- A verdict that rises as pending results land adds a row and never edits one, and the claim's `verdict_id` names its newest verdict
- A FAIL says where it points: the file and line of each stack frame, the code its failing test covers, and a journey's first step that differs from the last PASS
- Whose checks count: a claim covered only by its own agent's checks never passes, and an agent's prediction for a check is recorded before the check runs
- One send-back per cause, and known failures keep running while waived, with each result recorded
- A spec check, or a check for behavior that must not change, that also fails on the merge base is BLOCKED as inherited, not FAIL; it becomes one fix task per cause, held by one session. A check for new or fixed behavior was proven to fail on the base, so it's never inherited: while it still fails on the claim's commit, the claim is FAIL
- Which checks run again on a new commit: those whose inputs changed, where a check's inputs are the paths it declares, or the whole commit if it declares none, plus the files its last runs read (#30); a changed path that no check's declared inputs cover reruns every check on the claim
- Numeric contracts: a check that compares computed numbers with a reference declares `contract`: the reference and the precision it computes in, the type the code under test must accumulate in, an absolute and a relative tolerance per output with their units, and a precision twin, the reference accumulating in a narrower type the contract names, put in place of the code under test. The check must fail on its twin at a named assertion, or it is INVALID, naming the twin's largest error; it compares every element of every output, and a compared count below an output's size (#30) makes it INVALID, naming the output. A requirement about computed numbers is covered only by a check with a contract, so a check of shapes, types or finiteness alone is too weak for it

### Fields
**[Verdict](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#verdict)**
- PASS, FAIL, INVALID, BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE, with the smallest failing case and where it points, pinned to a commit and, on a workspace, to the digests of what its state sources read. It shows as one line in the chat at the stop.
- It can never: Be written by an agent or an extension

**[Requirement outcome](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#requirement-outcome)**
- Inside `verdict.made`: `requirements: [{req: req handle, outcome: PASS | FAIL | INVALID | BLOCKED | INCONCLUSIVE | pending, check, depth, oracle: code | model | person, runs: {clean: u16, needed: u16, counted: [run handle]}, smallest, points_to, evidence: [sha256], proof: statement | static_check | test_run | journey | decision, ask: ask handle (optional)}]`
- It can never: Be written by an agent or an extension; color a chip with nothing behind it

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Property tests cover every precedence pair
- [ ] p = 10% needs 29 clean runs; p = 45% needs 6, since 0.55⁵ is 5.03%, above 5%; a count that rounds ln 0.05 / ln 0.55 = 5.01 down to 5 fails this test
- [ ] A different error than the accepted one still fails
- [ ] A new commit makes the old verdict stale
- [ ] A FAIL names the file and line of each stack frame and the first journey step that differs from the last PASS
- [ ] A claim covered only by its own agent's checks never passes
- [ ] Three failures with one cause make one send-back
- [ ] A check that fails on one real run and passes on another of the same commit is INCONCLUSIVE with the failing runs attached, never FAIL or PASS; one that fails every real run is FAIL; and a timing check's run under load counts neither way
- [ ] A fix claim whose own check, proven to fail on the base, still fails on every real run of the claim's commit is FAIL with its smallest failing case, never BLOCKED as inherited; when `npm test` also fails on the base for another cause, the claim is still FAIL, and that failure becomes one inherited fix task instead of joining the send-back
- [ ] On a red main, a claim whose only failures are inherited is BLOCKED with one fix task per cause, never FAIL
- [ ] A claim with no check selected, or with a requirement no check covers, is INVALID naming that requirement, never PASS; a requirement covered at its depth only by the agent's own passing check is INCONCLUSIVE with one ask to approve that check, never INVALID or PASS
- [ ] With a unit check that fails and a six-minute journey still running, the claim is FAIL at once and its agent is sent back inside the hold; with the unit check passing, the claim stays pending until the journey lands, with no INCONCLUSIVE verdict or open item for the running journey; and while a requirement waits on your taste answer, a missing secret makes the claim BLOCKED at once with one unblock ask for the secret and none for the taste call
- [ ] Every run ends as passed, failed, ran nothing, missing, overran, stopped or uncounted, and a check runner that returns anything else, or a verdict, fails conformance; a missing run makes its check BLOCKED with the cause, an overran one counts as a failed run, a stopped one makes its check INCONCLUSIVE, and one that ran nothing INVALID; a stub runner that crashes mid-run leaves its run stopped, never failed or ran nothing, while a test that crashes under it is failed
- [ ] A check with p = 10% that fails on its first run of a commit and passes on its second is INCONCLUSIVE at once, its open item names no runs still needed, and no third run of it starts on that commit
- [ ] A requirement that needs a journey, covered by a passing unit test and a passing journey, is PASS; covered by the passing unit test alone, it is INVALID, naming the depth it needs
- [ ] A BLOCKED claim with a missing secret records one open item naming the evidence that would close it; raised again it stays one record, and a flaky check's INCONCLUSIVE open item adds nothing to Needs you
- [ ] On a claim with check A declaring `src/**` and check B declaring `docs/**`, both passing, a commit that changes only `scripts/build.sh` reruns A and B, and a commit that changes only `src/a.ts` reruns A and keeps B's result; a selection that matches changed paths only against declared inputs reruns nothing for `scripts/build.sh` and carries both old results to the new commit, which this test fails
- [ ] Check C declares `fixtures/**`, and test check T declares `src/**` and read `fixtures/prices.json` on its last run; a commit that only changes a price in that fixture, so that T's assertion breaks, reruns C and T, and the claim is FAIL naming T; a selection by declared inputs alone reruns only C, keeps T's old PASS and fails this test
- [ ] After a failed run of a check whose needed runs aren't reached, up to two more runs start, and a pass among them ends its runs: if every real run failed, the check is FAIL, and a pass makes it INCONCLUSIVE
- [ ] An overran run counts as a failed run: two more runs start, three overruns make the check FAIL naming its deadline, and an overrun with a pass makes it INCONCLUSIVE
- [ ] A check that was INCONCLUSIVE on the parent commit stays INCONCLUSIVE on a new commit that changes none of its inputs, with no new run; a commit that changes one of its inputs runs it again
- [ ] Budgets, on the reference Mac in the local preflight, compared with the merge base: a verdict from 1,000 runs is computed in under 10 ms
- [ ] A known failure past its expiry date fails again
- [ ] Every rule is tested and the highest by precedence wins: a claim with one check BLOCKED as inherited and another that failed on every real run is FAIL, and one with a check missing a secret and another that ran nothing is INVALID; an engine that returns the first rule that matches, in the order the design lists them, returns BLOCKED for both and fails this test
- [ ] A claim BLOCKED at once on a missing secret, whose unit check then fails on every real run, becomes FAIL as a new verdict row: the BLOCKED row stays as it was, and the claim's `verdict_id` names the FAIL; a projection that rewrites the BLOCKED row in place keeps one row and fails this test, naming the claim
- [ ] On a red main where `npm test` fails `cart.test.ts › rounds tax` on the base, a claim whose `npm test` fails that test and also `checkout.test.ts › applies coupon`, which passes on the base, is FAIL naming the coupon test; one that fails only the tax test is BLOCKED as inherited. An engine that judges inheritance per check returns BLOCKED for the first and fails this test
- [ ] A reference verdict function in test code agrees with the engine on 10,000 seeded generated claims, and the properties listed in How runs become one of five verdicts hold. An engine that ranks pending below PASS, or keys a result by commit alone, fails, naming the generated case
- [ ] A PASS on Node 20 doesn't carry to the same commit run on Node 22, nor to a journey whose viewport changed from 1280×720 to 1440×900. A cache keyed by commit and check digest alone carries both and fails this test
- [ ] p = 1% needs 299 and p = 95% needs exactly 1; p = 0, p = 100%, p = −5% and p = 10 with no unit each make the check BLOCKED naming the value; a check with no `runs` or `accept` needs 1. `Math.ceil(Math.log(0.05)/Math.log(1 − p))` returns 2 for p = 95% and needs no runs for 0 and 100%, so it fails this test
- [ ] Check A passed a claim at commit C 35 days ago, and retention has removed its evidence. A new claim at commit D, which changes no path A reads, runs A again instead of carrying it; when that run fails, the new claim's verdict is FAIL, and the old claim's verdict row, its runs and its verdict record hash are unchanged. An engine that carries A's result to D fails, and one that adds the new FAIL to the old claim fails, each naming the claim
- [ ] Each requirement outcome in `verdict.made` lists the runs it counted by handle: when check B's PASS at commit C carries to commit D because none of B's inputs changed, B's requirement on D lists B's run at C, and the reference function recomputes D's verdict from exactly the listed runs; an engine that lists only runs made on D leaves B with no run and fails this test, naming the requirement
- [ ] With every other check passed, a claim whose journey never started, because its stop was answered "proceed" and the next claim changed the journey's inputs, is pending and reads stale, never PASS and never INVALID, with no open item for the journey; a claim whose journey never started because its reproduction check failed is FAIL naming that check, with no INVALID for the journey. An engine that reads a check with no run as one that ran nothing makes the first INVALID, and one that leaves the check out makes it PASS, and each fails this test, naming the claim
- [ ] On a fixture whose precision twin, a float64 reference accumulating in FP16, differs from the FP32 answer by at most 4e-3, a check with contract `{accumulate: fp32, atol: 1e-3, rtol: 1e-3, twin: {accumulate: fp16}}` fails on the twin at its named `assert_close` and counts, while the same check with `atol: 1e-2` passes the twin and is INVALID, naming 4e-3. A check whose only assertions are that the output has the expected shape and that every value is finite doesn't cover a requirement about computed numbers, so that requirement is INVALID, naming the depth it needs. An engine that never runs the twin, or counts the shape check as cover, fails this test

### Added Oct 9
- Proof depth: each approved feature or journey names the depth it needs (unit, integration, journey, live). A deeper proof satisfies a shallower one, never the reverse, and a check too weak for the claim is INVALID for it.
- Coverage: each check lists the claim IDs it covers. The verdict is computed per claim and rolled up by a validator; agents never write verdict fields; a claim nothing covers can't pass.

One long-running process per user that owns the record and answers hook calls.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [One hub per user, a tiny hook client, and extensions in-process](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#one-hub-per-user-a-tiny-hook-client-and-extensions-in-process) · [Socket roles and contract versions](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#socket-roles-and-contract-versions) · [How it installs](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#how-it-installs) · [Threats, and what stops each one](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#threats-and-what-stops-each-one) · [Hook protocol (deep-hook and the hub)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#hook-protocol-deep-hook-and-the-hub)

### Scope
- Listens on `~/.deepbuild/hub.sock` with mode 0600
- Single writer to the record; per-session queues
- Runs as a per-user service that starts at login (launchd on macOS, a systemd user service on Linux, a per-user logon task on Windows); it ignores hangups, records why it stopped, refuses a second start through a lock the OS holds and releases when the process dies, never a PID file, and replays from the log after a crash
- Health endpoint for `deep doctor`
- Clients reach the hub at an address, a local socket today, and none assumes the hub is on the same machine, so it can later run on a machine you own. A hub with no project members listens on no network port, as the criterion below holds it; once a project has members it also listens on the one TLS port the hub.listen setting names (#1338)
- A worktree of DeepBuild itself can run a dev hub with `deep hub start --root <folder>`: its own socket, ledger, evidence and control token, with ports from leases; deep-hook and `deep mcp` keep using the installed hub unless you opt a worktree's sessions in with `deep hub use --root <folder>`, a control command that, like `deep off`, takes effect only once the OS confirms you (#19) and that deep-hook denies to an agent's call (#17)
- Sequence numbers: the hub reads each `seq` as a canonical decimal string into a `bigint`, refuses one outside 0 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 or in any other form, a JSON number included, naming the field and why, and writes it back as the same string in every reply that carries it, to the app, the CLI and `deep mcp`; it never parses `seq` as a JavaScript number
- Parsing off the event loop: a worker thread parses each hook request line, keeps its kind's catalogue fields, scrubs them and hashes what goes to evidence, as it does each transcript line read for a backfill or a tail; the event loop only reads lines, acknowledges, routes and writes replies
- Owns the evidence store (#15): each connection writes evidence through a writer bound to its role, so a file from `deep.evidence.put`, `deep_evidence` or the app's paste takes its origin from the credential, never the payload; a run's text evidence is scrubbed of the values the hub injected or holds by handle and of the env it passed to that process; the hub runs the store's retention pass at start and daily, with the hashes decisions cite and the hashes `transcript.archived` events link, read from the record; and a file leaves only through the store's send, with the ask router answering its asks

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Two hub starts at once leave exactly one hub running
- [ ] deep-hook, `deep mcp`, the app and the CLI take the hub's address from one setting, and each passes its tests against a hub reached through a forwarded socket
- [ ] Cut at each durable write point the storage interface numbers in a scripted 200-event scenario, every restart keeps every FULL commit, no ID twice, no `log_pos` reused and every spooled event once, with projections equal to their rebuild. A check run in flight records `stopped`, cause hub restarted, and its claim's checks run again
- [ ] The socket isn't readable by another user
- [ ] A hub killed with `kill -9` leaves no lock that blocks the next start, and a stale PID file from another program never stops the hub from starting
- [ ] A dev hub started from a worktree with its own root runs beside the installed hub, and sessions that didn't opt in still reach the installed one
- [ ] Closing the terminal or SSH session that started the hub leaves it running, with the secret store and the network still reachable, and every stop records its reason
- [ ] When an append fails, as on a full disk, the hub stops acknowledging claims and every gate turns watch-only with a BLOCKED reason until appends work again
- [ ] An event that claims a session it can't be checked against (its transcript, working folder or process tree) is recorded as unverified and never takes over that session

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [Evidence](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#evidence) · [Privacy](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#privacy)

### Scope
- `~/.deepbuild/evidence/ab/cdef…` layout with type and size recorded in the log
- Redaction of keys, tokens and secret-shaped strings in text evidence, and by exact value: for each run the hub keeps in memory the values it injected or holds by handle and the values of the environment variables it passes to a process when a variable's name marks a secret (it contains `TOKEN`, `KEY`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or `AUTH`), its value matches a secret pattern, or its value is one word of 16 characters or more that isn't a path (short plain values such as `CI=true`, `NODE_ENV=test`, `TZ=UTC` or a leased port stay), and scrubs them in raw, base64 and URL-encoded forms, base64 at all three byte offsets and in both the standard and URL-safe alphabets, across chunk boundaries, before any evidence is hashed
- Retention: 30 days by default, kept forever when a decision cites it or a `transcript.archived` event links it; a series' uncited batch files leave after 24 hours and its uncited minute rollups after 7 days (#262); the newest `layer.rows` file for each installed layer, parent and level is kept while the layer is installed (#259)
- Derived files, such as a highlighted screenshot, record the hash of the file they came from
- Each piece of evidence carries a redaction label and a license; a video keeps each step's start and end time, so a receipt opens it at that step
- Binary evidence checked at intake: a screenshot, a video frame or a recording must match the type its slot declares by its leading bytes and have its end (a PNG's `IEND` chunk, a JPEG's end-of-image marker, an MP4's boxes adding up to the file with `moov` among them); one cut short is kept as truncated, naming what's missing, and one of another type is refused, so its slot reads truncated or missing, never captured
- Each file records its origin from the writer's connection, never from the call: made by DeepBuild (a render, a capture, a journey, a job's output or an export), chosen by you in the app (a paste, a drop or a file picker), or put there by an agent; a file made from others, such as a job's output, keeps origin agent when any of its inputs was put there by an agent. A file leaves the machine only by hash, never by path; one an agent put there leaves only after an ask that names its hash and destination, asked once for that pair; and every receipt lists what went out, by hash and destination

### Fields
**[Evidence](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#evidence-1)**
- `{sha256, kind, source, origin: deepbuild | you | agent, redaction: complete | incomplete | unknown, license}`. `origin` comes from the writer's connection, never from the call, and a file made from others keeps `agent` when any input has it. Its redaction is `complete` on text the scrub in Privacy has cleared, `incomplete` on output the scrub couldn't clear and on a journey's screenshots and video after the journey types a secret into a field that isn't a password field, and `unknown` on a capture of the screen, a window, the camera or the microphone.
- It can never: Leave the machine by path; leave when an agent put it there, unless you approved its hash for that destination; or leave in an export while its redaction is anything but `complete`, unless you approve

The `events` table is the source of truth. Every other table is a projection the hub can rebuild by replaying it.

**Epic:** #1 · **Design:** [One event log, with tables built from it](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#one-event-log-with-tables-built-from-it) · [Projections the canvas reads](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/canvas-primitives.md#projections-the-canvas-reads) · [Privacy](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#privacy) · [Hooks are evidence, not a state machine](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#hooks-are-evidence-not-a-state-machine) · [Hook protocol (deep-hook and the hub)](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#hook-protocol-deep-hook-and-the-hub)

### Scope
- `events` table (STRICT, WAL, ULID ids) with schema-validated `data`
- Projections: sessions, commits, claims, checks, runs, verdicts, asks, decisions, leases (with a mode), definitions (one per ask, shared by every attempt) and attempts
- `actor` and `scope` columns on events, set by the hub from the connection's credential, never from the payload
- Forward-only migrations
- `better-sqlite3` behind a small storage interface
- More projections: tasks, open items, notices, readings, plans, dry merges, and each session's changed files
- `seq` stored as an SQLite INTEGER, from 0 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807, and read back exactly as a `bigint` through better-sqlite3's safe integers, never as a JavaScript number; the record's JSON and evidence carry it as its decimal string
- Identity and order: an event's ID is its identity, the ULID deep-hook minted for a hook's event, kept through the spool and every replay and appended once. Each event belongs to one turn: the one its agent's turn ID names, for a tool event the one its call began in, and otherwise the one open when it arrives. Events order by `seq` within their turn, and two with the same `seq` are both kept in the order of their IDs, a fixed order every replay repeats that never says which came first. A stamp never moves an event before the start of its turn or into an earlier one: an event stamped that early, as when the clock steps back, keeps its arrival place, and the session shows a "clock went back" reading. A tool event that arrives after its turn's Stop is recorded in that turn and never reopens it
- Log position: each event gets a `log_pos`, its position in the event log, when the hub appends it, an integer only the hub assigns that only grows and is never reused, kept apart from the event's ID and its `seq`. Positions come from a block the hub records with `synchronous=FULL` before using any of it, so a power cut can skip log positions but never hands one out twice; a replayed spool's events take new log positions; each event takes its `log_pos` inside the commit that writes it, so positions commit in order and a gap a consumer sees never fills later; and a payload that carries its own `log_pos` is refused
- Evidence in the record: each file the evidence store (#15) stores appends `evidence.put` with its hash, kind, type, size, origin, redaction, license, the hashes it was made from and a recording's step times, and each file its retention pass removes appends evidence.removed; the `evidence` projection (hash, kind, redaction, license, step_times) is built from them and replaces the store's interim journal, and your yes to a send is read back from the `asks` projection

### Fields
**[Event](https://github.com/windoliver/deepbuild/blob/main/docs/technical-design.md#event)**
- The only state the kernel keeps: `{id, kind, subject, writer, actor, scope, data, ts}`, with the writer taken from the connection and the actor and scope from its credential, and a `log_pos`, its position in the event log, that the hub assigns at append. Its kinds include these shapes:
  - `user.ask`, for each prompt and each message typed while the agent works;
  - `session.child_started`;
  - `claim.made`, with its scope: a session, a child or a task;
  - `task.created`;
  - `worktree.created` and `worktree.removed`;
  - `doc.patched`.
  Only the core appends the kinds that record a decision: `verdict.made` and `verdict.stale` from its verdict engine, `definition.locked` and `definition.revised` from its definition lock, and `decision.created`, `decision.applied`, `ask.answered` and `ask.defaulted` from the trusted path, its check of a resolver's answer and an ask's deadline. `deep.record.append` refuses each of them from every other writer, a first-party extension in the hub included, naming the kind, and the extension host's kit holds a planted first-party extension that tries.
- It can never: Carry a writer it claims rather than one its connection proves, or a `log_pos` the hub didn't assign; or record a verdict, a locked definition, a decision or an answer from any writer but the core
